era_policy.principle: Group by major content era, not every patch release.
era_policy.note: Exactly 13 user-defined eras: 1.0 through 1.9, then 2.0, 2.1, and 2.2. All 2.2-derived patches stay in the single 2.2 bucket.

object_catalog.requirement: Record the objects available in each era, with object ID, category, first known version, availability evidence, and changes/removal notes.
object_catalog.rule: Do not mark an object as available or validated without evidence; distinguish object existence from whether it can be placed in the editor.

official_robtop.inclusion: All available official RobTop levels, using RobsVault as the collection/reference source, including spin-off levels and beta variants when their identity/version can be established.

rated_online_community.inclusion: Target exactly 1,820 community examples across 13 eras × 14 analytical difficulty/mode cohorts × 10 examples. Use rated online community levels where available; where early eras lack enough eligible levels or a category did not exist, use randomly selected Gauntlet levels as explicitly flagged substitutes.
rated_online_community.selection_goal: The coolest/most instructive levels: prioritize creativity, gameplay quality, representative techniques, and diversity rather than popularity alone.
rated_online_community.coverage_rule: Track progress with a 13-era × 14-cohort × 10-example matrix. Fill with eligible rated community levels first; use Gauntlet substitutes only when necessary and record their true release era. Do not claim completion until all 1,820 entries, rating/era metadata, and native level data are verified.

gauntlet_fallback.trigger: An early-era difficulty cell lacks enough eligible rated community levels, or that difficulty category did not yet exist in the era.
gauntlet_fallback.selection: Randomly select Gauntlet levels to fill remaining slots.
gauntlet_fallback.analysis_rule: Do not mislabel a Gauntlet substitute as a level originating in the historical era being studied; preserve its actual release era and flag it as a substitute.

mandatory_selection_policy.rule: Every named mandatory level must be included in the corpus if its identity and level data can be verified. Mandatory examples count toward the 1,200 target rather than being added on top of it, unless the corpus accounting later explicitly chooses otherwise.
mandatory_selection_policy.historical_coverage: Include many influential early-era levels by Darnoc and Neptune, prioritizing historically important and representative levels while preserving actual release era and creator attribution.
mandatory_selection_policy.relevance_selection: After mandatory levels, fill remaining slots with historically relevant and technically instructive rated levels, not merely random popular picks.
mandatory_selection_policy.verification: Verify exact level identity, creator, rating/difficulty, release/era, and availability of native level data; do not silently substitute similarly named levels.

categories: N/A (reference only; not eligible as rated training data)
difficulty_categories.policy: These are 14 analytical cohorts, not 14 difficulty icons that all existed in every update. Platformer Moon cohorts are analytical groupings, not separate official classic difficulty icons. Preserve historical difficulty taxonomy and mark cohorts that did not yet exist.
difficulty_categories.note: The 14-cohort matrix is a research-accounting structure. Early-era gaps use the documented Gauntlet substitution rule; substitutes must not be mislabeled as historical levels.

analysis_targets: Object vocabulary and object placement patterns
Differences between eras and between official and community design
data_integrity: Store provenance and verification state for every object and level.
Screenshots/videos may aid visual analysis but do not replace native level data for learning object placement.
Do not claim the corpus is complete until coverage and source data have been checked.
Mandatory named levels and creator-attribution requirements must be tracked as explicit inclusion checks in the corpus matrix.
status: specification and importer committed; collection not complete. The importer can populate names/IDs from public metadata, but native level strings and historical release/rating dates still require verification.
